claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Great! Let me start by asking you about your child or children.

**How old is the child (or children) you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

Please tell me:
- The name(s) of the child/children
- Their age(s)

This will help me determine which path to take through the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who's 16 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 16 years old.

Since Alex is 16-19 years old, I need to check whether they're in full-time education or approved training. This is an important factor for eligibility at this age.

**Can you tell me - is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training?**

(Full-time education typically means school, college, or university. Approved training includes schemes like apprenticeships or other government-approved training programmes.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. They left school and aren't studying anything right now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. Since Alex has left education and isn't in any training, let me check if they might still be eligible under an extension provision.

**When did Alex leave school?** (Approximately - was it within the last few weeks, months, or longer ago?)

This matters because there are some time-limited extensions for young people who have recently left full-time education.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, now I understand the next requirement. For Alex to remain eligible after leaving school, there's a special extension available, but it has specific conditions:

**20-Week Extension Eligibility:**

There's a 20-week extension available if:
1. Alex left approved education or training
2. **AND** Alex has registered with a qualifying service (such as a government careers service, Connexions, or the armed services)

**So I need to ask you:**

1. **When exactly did Alex leave school?** (How many weeks ago? Is it within the last 20 weeks?)
2. **Has Alex registered with any of these services:**
   - A government careers service?
   - Connexions?
   - The armed services?

If both conditions are met, Alex can continue to receive Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from leaving school.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't registered with any careers service or anything like that. They just left school and haven't signed up for any of those services.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Eligibility Outcome: NOT ELIGIBLE**

Unfortunately, **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

### **Why:**

Alex is 16 years old and has left full-time education without being in approved training. While there is a provision that allows a 20-week extension for young people in this situation, it only applies if they **register with a qualifying service** such as:
- A government careers service
- Connexions
- The armed services

Since Alex hasn't registered with any of these services, the extension doesn't apply, meaning Alex no longer meets the definition of a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit.

### **What could change this:**

If Alex were to:
1. **Join full-time education** (such as college, university, or an approved training course), OR
2. **Register with a careers service, Connexions, or the armed services** (which would give a 20-week extension from when they left school)

Then they could become eligible again for Child Benefit.

### **Next Steps:**

If you have questions about how to register with a careers service, you can contact your local Connexions service or government careers advice service for more information.

If you believe your circumstances have changed or you have additional information, feel free to get in touch, and I can reassess your eligibility.
